safety.note: The model's stated harm was prolonged B-cell depletion; the only toxicity ever noted in the treated mice was a lack of B cells.

safety.judgement: Results: 'The only toxicity ever noted in the treated mice was a lack of B cells.' Yescarta clinical review 4.3: 'The mice did not show any overt signs of toxicity.' Dated 2010 (rule 6, earliest public date): the Kochenderfer 2010 FL case report (https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2010-04-281931, epub 2010-07-28) already showed prolonged B-lineage elimination and very low immunoglobulins, after the model paper; the 2012 paper stays the source of the stated comparison. Tolerability ruling: the mice 'did not show any overt signs of toxicity' (Yescarta clinical review), a stated safety prediction; FL patient 8 had severe cytokine toxicity, a harm a mouse cannot show, so the held B-cell prediction keeps same, partial.

safety.judgement: Stated prediction (B-cell depletion) held: the Introduction puts murine and clinical B-cell eradication side by side ('Similar to the murine studies ... Ag-specific eradication of normal B cells has been demonstrated'). The paper's headline harm, cytokine-associated toxicity (FL patient 8, Table 4: hypotension, obtundation, acute renal failure, capillary leak syndrome), was never shown by the mice, and no source says the model missed it (WebFetch of the full text: NOT FOUND). v2 scored that silence contra. v3 says a mouse cannot show cytokine release so its silence on CRS is not a miss, and the myeloma BCMA tile applies the same rule to CAR-T, so this stays same. Alternative reading: this C3H model is immunocompetent and later mouse systems (tracks below) did show CRS, so the silence was a model-design miss; under that reading this entry is contra at 2011, comparison_stated false. Later FL trials, no model comparison: ZUMA-5 iNHL CRS 84% (grade >=3 8%), neurologic toxicities 77% (grade >=3 21%) (Yescarta label); TRANSCEND FL CRS 58% (grade >=3 1%), neurological events 15% (Morschhauser 2024); RELIANCE no grade >=3 CRS.

safety.judgement: First prospective test of the model's prediction with a member drug (decision 10), scored as usual. The model predicted prevention of CRS and a significant reduction in neuroinflammation; with lenzilumab 4/6 patients had CRS and 5/6 neurologic events (serious encephalopathy 3/6, serious aphasia 1/6), against ZUMA-1's 93% CRS and 64% neurologic events for axi-cel alone, so not prevented and no evident reduction: contra in direction at low confidence. Humanigen's press release of 2021-04-20 (tier 5, the earliest public report) framed the same six patients as positive (no severe CRS or neurotoxicity at 1800 mg; one 2-day grade-3 neurotoxicity at 600 mg; ORR 83%); the registry is the higher-tier record of the same trial and sets the status, and dating by the press release would move this entry to 2021 with the status unchanged. Alternative reading: same with source_calls_it partial, on grade >=3 CRS 0/6 and grade >=3 neurotoxicity 1/6 against ZUMA-1's 13% and 28%, which n=6 cannot distinguish from no effect.
